title: `demolish node` with no name reads fields[2] out of bounds — harness panics instead of returning a parse error
detail: A demo line `demolish node` (two fields) passes the len(fields)<2 guard, then indexes fields[2], which does not exist. The parser's stated contract is malformed input = parse error, not crash; this panics the whole harness run.
recommended_fix: Guard the node branch with len(fields) >= 3 before reading fields[2], returning the same 'demolish a-b|node name' parse error otherwise.

title: Malformed `within` window is silently coerced to 0..0 instead of a parse error
detail: When rest[1] does not split into exactly two parts ("within 100", "within 1..2..3") no error is returned: lo_ms/hi_ms stay 0, narrowing the expectation to tick 0. Trailing tokens after a valid window are also ignored. Violates the header's 'never silent coercions' contract.
recommended_fix: Add an else branch returning a 'bad window' parse error when len(range) != 2, and reject leftover tokens after a valid window.

title: Replay gate always boots the six-node map — bare-fixture demos replay against the wrong fixture
evidence:
+	// the fixture flag is carried by the demo; bare demos don't reach here
+	// with commands, but replay the same way
+	bar := false
+	_ = bar
+	replayed, ok := replay_hashes(log_path, catalogs, u64(len(live_hashes)), false, &fails)

+// bare selects the empty-map fixture (the log doesn't record the fixture; the demo does)
+replay_hashes :: proc(log_path: string, catalogs: ^pp.Catalogs, ticks: u64, bare: bool, fails: ^[dynamic]string) -> ([dynamic]u64, bool) {
...
+	rc: prun.Run_Context
+	if bare {
+		prun.run_context_create_bare(&rc, header.seed, catalogs)
+	} else {
+		prun.run_context_create(&rc, header.seed, catalogs)
+	}

+			rep_ok := verify_replay(name, log_path, catalogs, hashes[:])
detail: main.odin calls verify_replay for every demo that passes T1 — bare demos included, with no fixture argument — but verify_replay hardcodes bare=false (run_replay does too), so replay boots the six-node map while the live run used run_context_create_bare. Bare demos' hashes diverge and the gate fails; the dead `bar` variable is the dropped flag.
recommended_fix: Thread demo.map_fixture through verify_replay/run_replay into replay_hashes' bare argument (delete bar), or record the fixture in the log header.

title: Captured frame image leaks in both T2 failure branches of check_golden
detail: rl.UnloadImage(img) runs only in the all-match branch. On mismatch>0 (and mismatch<0, which passes {} instead) the captured image — whose buffer was LoadImageColors-allocated in swizzle_rb — goes to save_diff_bundle, which only samples it, so every failing frame leaks its pixel buffer. Failing frames are the harness's main workload.
recommended_fix: Call rl.UnloadImage(img) in the mismatch<0 and mismatch>0 branches after save_diff_bundle, mirroring the missing-golden branch.

title: Diff image data is Odin temp-allocator memory, freed by raylib's UnloadImage (cross-allocator free)
evidence:
+		out := make([]rl.Color, n, context.temp_allocator)
...
+		dimg.data = raw_data(out)
...
+		rl.UnloadImage(dimg)
detail: out is allocated with Odin's temp allocator; dimg.data points at it; rl.UnloadImage(dimg) frees image.data with raylib's allocator. Freeing arena memory through free() is undefined behavior — heap corruption/crash on every diff-bundle write, i.e. every T2 failure.
recommended_fix: Allocate out with context.allocator and delete it with Odin after ExportImage, or skip UnloadImage for an image whose data it doesn't own; never mix allocators.

title: core:strconv imported in goldens.odin but never referenced anywhere in the file
detail: Every procedure body in goldens.odin uses only fmt/os/strings/rl/pp/rnd/prun; strconv appears nowhere in the file. Odin builds that flag unused imports refuse to compile the harness; at minimum it is a dead import.
recommended_fix: Remove the core:strconv import line from goldens.odin.

title: write_file and write_log are byte-identical duplicate procedures in goldens.odin
detail: Two identical procedures with identical comments in the same file; main.odin calls write_log while goldens.odin calls write_file. A fix applied to one silently misses the other — a drift hazard.
recommended_fix: Collapse to a single write_file used from main.odin too, or give write_log a distinct purpose.

title: Unreachable duplicate os.exists check left in check_golden
detail: The preceding if !os.exists(path) branch returns, so this second check can never execute — leftover from an earlier draft.

title: Intents scheduled after the last tick frame are queued but never applied — the audit only counts submissions
detail: Ticks fire only at frames where frame % frames_per_tick == 0 (e.g. run_ms=550, hz=10: last tick at frame 30). An intent at frame 33 is submitted via bus_submit after the last tick; no later step applies it, and the audit compares intent_idx (submission count) only, so the drop is silent.
recommended_fix: Track the last stepped frame and flag intents whose frame exceeds it, or reject intents past the final tick at parse time.

title: Lint gate 2 regex cannot match file-scope `x := 5` declarations — globals slip through
detail: The pattern requires ':' followed by whitespace; in `x := 5` the colon is followed by '='. The ODN-13 'no globals' gate therefore passes exactly the most common file-scope declaration form it claims to forbid.
recommended_fix: Extend the regex to also match ':=' (e.g. '^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*[ ]*:=?[ ]'), and account for constants/procs being excluded by existing filters.

title: Lint gate 4 only matches a bare `_ = ` at line start — `x, _ :=` and `_, _ :=` discards pass
detail: The regex requires the line to start with '_' then ' = '. Multi-value discards like `x, _ := f()` or `_, _ := f()` start with other characters and use ':=', so dropped error returns in the common compound form are never flagged.
recommended_fix: Widen the pattern to catch compound discards (e.g. '(_|\w+, )_ :=' plus the bare form) or accept and document the heuristic's blind spot.

title: A bare `capture` line with no times is silently accepted as zero captures
detail: `capture` or `capture at` yields an empty rest; the split produces one empty part which is skipped, and no error is raised. A typo'd capture directive silently records nothing, contrary to the header's strict-parse contract.
recommended_fix: Return a parse error when no capture time survives parsing.

title: `harness save` exits 0 and prints 'blessed' even when expectation checks failed during the bless
detail: run_demo returns ok || save, so expectation failures during a bless never increment failures and the 'FAILED during bless' branch is unreachable for them; save mode also skips the FAIL printout and write_report. A failed run is blessed silently with exit 0.
recommended_fix: Print and count failures in save mode too (return ok, not ok || save), so a bless that fails expectations exits non-zero.

title: build_raylib_sw.sh header says 'release tarball' but the script git-clones, and an interrupted clone is treated as complete
evidence:
+# raylib 6.0 release tarball; cached under tools/raylib-sw/ (gitignored).
...
+if [ ! -d "$SRC" ]; then
+  mkdir -p "$WORK"
+  echo "-- fetching raylib $RAYLIB_TAG source"
+  git clone --depth 1 --branch "$RAYLIB_TAG" https://github.com/raysan5/raylib.git "$SRC"
+fi
detail: Comment/implementation mismatch (tarball vs git tag clone), and the existence of $SRC — not clone success — gates the fetch, so a partial clone silently builds a broken raylib and every later run reuses it.
recommended_fix: Update the comment, and verify clone success (check for $SRC/src/raylib.h, or clone to a temp dir and rename on success).
